items.title: AI-smell prose keeps shipping
items.why: 8 independent atone events across em-dashes in owner replies, vague PR bodies, and audit-register RCAs show text reminders have not moved this count; guard-prose-quality.sh and guard-ai-signature.sh exist but the em-dash case specifically has no blocking Stop hook.

proposal.change: Register prose-smell-stop.sh as a Stop hook so em-dash and audit-register patterns block delivery rather than only recording after the fact.

items.title: Dense briefings outnumber direct answers
items.why: 9 atone events for the same shape (status report leading with what-I-did, restatements of settled plans, word salad) despite the dense-briefing rule; dense-briefing-shapes-stop.sh exists on disk but rg finds zero registration in settings.json.

proposal.change: Register dense-briefing-shapes-stop.sh (already at ~/.claude/scripts/hooks/dense-briefing-shapes-stop.sh) as a Stop hook — the script exists and has tests but is not wired.

items.title: Names next work then stops
items.why: 8 atone events for halting after narrating the next step despite never-halt-on-authority-you-hold being an always-loaded rule; named-next-work-stop.sh exists on disk but rg finds zero registration in settings.json.

proposal.change: Register named-next-work-stop.sh as a Stop hook — the script and tests exist at ~/.claude/scripts/hooks/named-next-work-stop.sh but are not wired into settings.json.

items.title: Declared done without running it
items.why: 5 atone events for claiming a path works without exercising it; declared-ready-stop.sh exists, rules/exercise-based-verification.md says it is muted by ~/.claude/.no-declared-ready-gate, but that mute file does not exist — meaning the gate is unregistered rather than deliberately silenced.

proposal.change: Register declared-ready-stop.sh as a Stop hook; the script exists at ~/.claude/scripts/hooks/declared-ready-stop.sh and the mute file ~/.claude/.no-declared-ready-gate is absent, so this is an unregistered gate, not a deliberately muted one.

items.title: RCAs anonymize known facts
items.why: The extractor blank-jobs RCA invented actor descriptions and removed named customers despite the facts being known; same session drew 4 owner corrections, indicating the writing pattern (vague euphemism) applies even when specifics are on hand.

proposal.change: Add an explicit constraint: when known actors, customers, or values are available, name them verbatim — anonymization is only for external-publication RCAs, never internal ones.

items.title: Asks owner for derivable values
items.why: 3 atone events (staging alias already in config, owner blocker list contradicted by memory, registry token already held) show the agent surfaces questions without checking stored context or config files first.

proposal.change: Extend guard-lazy-question.sh to detect questions whose answer is resolvable from memory files or a single grep of the project config before the question reaches the owner.

items.title: Prompt fill replaced owner text
items.why: atone:mist-20261006-082745-b9 records that gcc-mods used mode:'replace' at 8 prompt-fill sites, destroying owner-typed text; affirm:aff-20261006-080735-a4 confirms the copy-path and attach escapes are the right pattern for other views.

proposal.change: Change all 8 prompt-fill insertions from mode:'replace' to mode:'insert' (or 'append') so owner-typed content is preserved; treat replace as an explicit opt-in only when the button label makes overwrite semantics obvious.

items.title: Staging alias question already in config
items.why: Covered by c-1f725c61 (asked for derivable value); the session-cluster framing adds no new pattern beyond what that repeat captures.

items.title: Pending items in session dump
items.why: Two owner corrections with pending items in core-dump is normal session volume with no distinguishing pattern beyond what c-ab3c677c and c-de1656a8 already cover.

items.title: pr-board/app.py hotspot
items.why: The three events span different slugs (staging-alias, declared-ready, prod landmine) that coincidentally touch the same file; no common failure mode internal to app.py itself is visible.

named.process_note: Four stop hooks (declared-ready-stop.sh, named-next-work-stop.sh, dense-briefing-shapes-stop.sh, prose-smell-stop.sh) appear on disk with tests but are absent from settings.json. The weekly reader would be more useful if it diffed the hooks/ directory against the registered Stop/PostToolUse entries in settings.json and surfaced the gap directly as a 'unregistered gate' cluster type — this would have caught all four in one structural row rather than requiring per-cluster grepping.
